claimBoundary: This task-local closure narrows rule evidence to every source-mapped atom on one exact Cryx/Nyrro roster state and separately records terminal relevance as ordering only. A bounded interval search may launch because every action is checked before execution and again against transition events; unknown atoms, unresolved atom relations and unresolved same-hook multi-atom ordering remain explicit [0,1] branches. Exact strategy values remain forbidden until those branches and the complete response/Chance/continuous domains close. Global unrelated-faction debt is context only.

rosterDependencyInventory.claimBoundary: This inventory includes every atom matched by an exact source ID or explicit atom key on the current roster state. It is a task dependency denominator, not terminal relevance pruning or proof that every interaction is certified.

selectedUnresolvedInteractions.relation: Each actual primary, AOE, spray, transferred, reaction-attack, or applicable legacy free-strike positive-damage receipt is consumed after its own complete attack; responses sharing that timing use active-player then inactive-player owner ordering together with Stumbling Drunk and other post-attack reactions.

A surviving model that actually marked positive damage from an enemy attack must roll one d3 after the complete attack and remove up to that many currently marked damage points, obeying damage-removal prohibitions and exact grid, spiral, or web semantics.
The exact self spell grants its canonical rule only while the spell status is active; the existing resource, spell targeting, trigger, interruption and movement or healing Host remains authoritative.

Last Word is ordered with Tough and other Disabled-stage triggers; it resolves only while its model remains in play, Disabled, and source-backed, then the ordinary lifecycle continues from the rechecked state.

The controller independently chooses an ordinary advance of up to three inches and one basic melee attack; movement geometry, free strikes, attack legality, damage, and nested lifecycle all use their canonical protocols.

each living model in the triggered unit independently chooses or declines its one three-inch Vengeance Move in controller order; only after every move choice resolves may any of those models choose one basic melee attack.

a_positive_damage_result from an enemy attack on one or more unit models persists as one exact unit trigger until that units next own Maintenance Phase, including when the initially damaged model is later destroyed.

every Vengeance Move uses ordinary advance path, terrain, model-blocker, free-strike, and reaction handling from the actual state, and the completed unit window consumes the one Vengeance Move allowed for each model that turn.
